cards.text: Jesus is speaking to the crowds and His disciples (Matthew 23:1). He's been warning that the scribes and Pharisees, the religious teachers who sit in Moses' seat, don't practice what they preach (Matthew 23:2-3). Then He doesn't hold back: "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites!"

cards.question: Jesus' first woe is about the kingdom of heaven. What does He say the scribes and Pharisees do with it?

answers.text: Open it only to their friends
Sell a place in it to the rich

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees enter the kingdom of heaven themselves.

cards.text: Woe number two. They traverse land and sea to win a single convert, and friend, I get winded hopping to the OVEN.

cards.question: Jesus says that when the scribes and Pharisees finally win that one convert, they make him something. What?

answers.text: Twice as much a son of hell as they are
A teacher twice as wise as they are
A servant who carries all their loads

cards.text: Woe number three, and Jesus calls them blind guides. They have rules about oaths, and these rules come with FINE PRINT: swear by the temple, they say, and it means nothing.

cards.question: But swear by the ___ of the temple, the scribes and Pharisees say, and you're bound by your oath.
Jesus asks the scribes and Pharisees which is greater, the gold or the temple. Why is the temple the greater one?

answers.text: The temple makes the gold sacred
The temple cost more than the gold
The temple is older than the gold

cards.text: They do the same thing with the altar: the altar means nothing, but the gift on it binds you. So Jesus asks, "Which is greater: the gift, or the altar that makes it sacred?"

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it.

cards.text: Then Jesus says whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by the One who dwells in it. All that FINE PRINT? Gone.

cards.question: Jesus says whoever swears by heaven swears by God's ___ and by the One who sits on it.

cards.text: Woe number four. They pay tithes of mint, dill, and cumin, and I bet somebody's counting every single DILL leaf.

cards.question: But Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees have disregarded the weightier matters of the law. What are they?
True or false: Jesus tells the scribes and Pharisees to stop tithing their mint, dill and cumin.

cards.text: Then He calls them blind guides again: "You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel." Picture somebody fishing one tiny bug out of their cup, then gulping down a whole CAMEL.

cards.question: What is Jesus saying about the scribes and Pharisees with the gnat and the camel?

answers.text: They fuss over tiny things and miss huge ones
They keep every rule both big and small
They care more about animals than people

cards.text: Woe number five. The scribes and Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish, and the outside is SPARKLING.

cards.question: Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and dish. What does He say is inside?
True or false: Jesus says to clean the inside of the cup and dish first, so the outside may become clean as well.

cards.text: Clean outside, greedy inside? That's a cookie box with a gorgeous bow on top and last month's crumbs inside. Woe number six: Jesus says they're like whitewashed tombs, which look beautiful on the outside.

cards.question: Jesus compares the scribes and Pharisees to whitewashed tombs. What are those tombs full of on the inside?
True or false: Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees look righteous on the outside but are full of hypocrisy and wickedness on the inside.

cards.text: Woe number seven: they build tombs for the prophets and decorate the monuments of the righteous. And they say if they'd lived in their fathers' days, they'd never have been partners in shedding the prophets' blood.

cards.question: When the scribes and Pharisees say they'd never have joined their fathers, what does Jesus say they testify against themselves?

answers.text: They're sons of those who murdered the prophets
They've never read what the prophets wrote
They want the prophets' places of honor

cards.text: Jesus says, "Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers." Then He calls them snakes, a brood of vipers.

cards.question: Jesus asks the scribes and Pharisees how they will escape the sentence of ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Because of this, I am sending you prophets and wise men and teachers." He says they will kill and crucify some of them, and flog others in their synagogues and persecute them from town to town.
Jesus says all the righteous blood shed on earth will come upon them. It starts with one righteous man and runs all the way to Zechariah son of Berechiah, murdered between the temple and the altar.

cards.question: Jesus says all the righteous blood shed on earth will come upon the scribes and Pharisees, from the blood of righteous ___ to the blood of Zechariah.

cards.text: Abel was Adam's son, killed by his brother Cain (Genesis 4:1-8). Then Jesus says, "Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation."
Then Jesus speaks to the city itself: "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her…" And He tells her how often He has longed to gather her children together.

cards.question: Jesus has longed to gather Jerusalem's children together. What picture does He use for it?

answers.text: A hen gathering her chicks under her wings
A shepherd carrying lambs in his arms
An eagle carrying its young on its wings

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says Jerusalem was willing to be gathered.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "Look, your house is left to you desolate." I think that one hurts to hear.

cards.question: Jesus tells Jerusalem they won't see Him again until they say, Blessed is He who comes in the name of the ___.
